A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TailedCore research work, with complete, readable main text and supplementary material. All 22 pages, including equations, figures, tables, proofs, and supplementary experiments, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TailedCore and TailSampler evaluations, ablations, robustness tests, and qualitative results in Section 6 and Supplementary Sections 10 and 12.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including evaluations on MVTecAD, VisA, and MVTec-LOCO. Retention from v1 does not change their status as original results.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains the same adaptive-angle class-size predictor, neighborhood voting, elbow-based tail selection, memory augmentation, and inference procedure. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both retain MVTecAD and VisA classification/segmentation, supplementary MVTec-LOCO structural/logical anomaly evaluation, and the same perturbed-tail and noisy-tail scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1-4 retain PaDiM, HVQ, WinCLIP, AnomalyCLIP, PatchCore, and SoftPatch. Corresponding supplementary experiments also retain SimpleNet, EfficientAD, UniAD, and the same clustering and outlier-detection comparators.

E3.justification: Dataset construction, test sets, AUROC metrics, model configurations, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. This includes the stated 10% training-noise protocol, Pareto and K=1/K=4 settings, and sample counts in Supplementary Tables 9-14.

E4.justification: The percentile/voting and memory-augmentation ablations, noise-ratio sweep, embedding analysis, and supplementary perturbation, noisy-tail, encoder, and qualitative analyses are retained unchanged (Tables 5-7; Figures 4-7).

E5.justification: Both retain five-seed benchmark means, Table 5's aggregation over 60 seeds, Figure 4's standard-deviation shading, and the same supplementary uncertainty reporting. No run-count or statistical-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and supplement. For example, Table 1 reports TailedCore's overall MVTecAD-Pareto image AUROC as 96.12% in both versions; supplementary result entries are likewise unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations are unchanged, including Supplementary Section 9's reflective-symmetry assumption, Proposition 1, and proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about TailSampler, TailedCore, mitigation of the tail-versus-noise dilemma, and comparative performance.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and limitations are unchanged, including dependence on discriminative embeddings and reflective symmetry, and difficulties with noisy tail classes and logical anomalies (Sections 6.5, 7, and Supplementary 10.2).

D1.justification: Implementation parameters, backbone descriptions, clustering and perturbation settings, dataset-generation details, and the abstract's code-repository link are unchanged. No additional reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 44 references are unchanged, preserving the same positioning relative to anomaly detection, long-tail noisy learning, and few-shot/outlier sampling.

P1.justification: v2 adds a project-lead marker to Jaewoo Park and expands the author footnote with 'Project lead,' while adjusting capitalization and punctuation. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the research prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-7 and Tables 1-26 retain their content, captions, formatting, and placement. Visual inspection confirms the same document layout, apart from the author-note and version-stamp text edits covered under P1.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies an author role but preserves the methods, evidence, theory, limitations, reproducibility information, and presentation of the research, including the supplement. This administrative clarification does not produce a meaningful overall change in paper quality.
